key.description:
Masked key — prefix plus the last 4 characters (e.g. `elfak_...245c`).
The full secret is never returned; use it only to tell two keys apart.

userId.description: Account bookkeeping. Retained for backwards compatibility; not part of the supported surface.

athenaEnabled.description: Whether this key is provisioned for Auto.

scopes.description:
Effective scopes for this key, including any enterprise overlay.

Scopes gate the `/v2` data and chat endpoints and every `/v3` endpoint
except `/v3/key-status`. They are NOT a complete access map: `/v2/auto/*`
is not scope-gated, so its reachability cannot be inferred from this array.

MentionV2.description:
A single sanitized mention returned by V2 data endpoints.

V2 never returns raw tweet text or content — use `link` to fetch the original
tweet if needed. `mentionedAt` is an ISO 8601 string.

tweetId.description: Tweet ID (string to preserve precision across 64-bit IDs).

mentionedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. "2026-04-18T15:07:49+00:00"). Not a unix timestamp.

repostBreakdown.description: Reposts broken down by audience: `smart` = smart accounts, `ct` = crypto-Twitter accounts.

KeywordMentionV2.description:
Mention returned by `/v2/data/keyword-mentions`. Includes minimal account
info; no follower counts, display name, bio, or account ID are returned.

tweetId.description: Tweet ID (string to preserve precision across 64-bit IDs).

mentionedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. "2026-04-18T15:07:49+00:00"). Not a unix timestamp.

repostBreakdown.description: Reposts broken down by audience: `smart` = smart accounts, `ct` = crypto-Twitter accounts.

account.description:
Minimal account info for the author. Only `username` and `isVerified` are
returned — no id, display name, follower count, or bio. May be omitted if
the underlying record is missing an account name.

metadata.description:
Pagination metadata. `cursor` is a millisecond timestamp — pass it back as
the `cursor` query param to fetch the next page. Omitted once `data` is
empty, which is the signal to stop paging. `total` is the complete
matching result set, not the remainder after the cursor, and may be
capped at 10000 for performance.

ChatSourceV2.description: A page the answer's research read. Links only: the page's content is not included.

kind.description:
What the link points at, read from its URL. Current values:
- `x_post` — a post on X
- `x_account` — an X profile
- `telegram` — a Telegram channel or message
- `dex` — a DEX pair or token page
- `explorer` — a block-explorer page (address, token, transaction)
- `prediction_market` — a Polymarket or Kalshi market
- `web` — any other page, such as a news article

A string rather than an enum so new kinds can ship without breaking
generated clients; treat a value you do not recognise as `web`.

title.description: What the research step did to reach this link, e.g. "Searched X".

sources.description:
Present only when the request set `includeSources: true`. Links the
research behind this answer read, in the order it read them, without
duplicates (at most 50). Empty when the answer used no linkable source.
A source was read, not necessarily cited in `message`.

symbol.description: Token ticker symbol (e.g. "BTC", "$ETH"). Required for tokenIntro / tokenAnalysis when contractAddress is not provided.

chain.description: Blockchain name (e.g. "ethereum", "solana"). Use together with contractAddress as an alternative to symbol.

contractAddress.description: Token contract address. Use together with chain as an alternative to symbol.

message.description: The user message. Required when analysisType is "chat"; ignored for all other analysis types.

sessionId.description: Omit to start a new conversation. Pass the sessionId from a previous response to continue an existing conversation.

analysisType.description:
The type of analysis to perform. Defaults to "chat".
- `chat` — conversational AI. Requires `message`.
- `macro` — macro market overview.
- `summary` — quick market summary.
- `tokenIntro` — token introduction. Requires `assetMetadata`.
- `tokenAnalysis` — in-depth token analysis. Requires `assetMetadata`.
- `accountAnalysis` — Twitter/X account analysis. Requires `assetMetadata.username`.

assetMetadata.description: Required for tokenIntro, tokenAnalysis, and accountAnalysis. See endpoint description for required fields per analysis type.

includeSources.description:
Set `true` to receive `data.sources`: the links the research behind the
answer read. Omitted or `false` leaves the response unchanged.

useMemory.description:
Set `true` to let this request use the saved memory of the Elfa account
that owns the API key: the answer can draw on notes from that account's
earlier chats, and this chat can add to them. Omitted or `false`, the
request neither reads nor writes saved memory. Has no effect when memory
is turned off in the account's chat settings. Leave it off when one key
serves many end users, so one user's notes never shape another's answer.

symbol.description: Ticker of the token or stock. A stock has an empty `chain` and `contractAddress`.

sessionId.description: Session ID for continuing this conversation

credits.description:
Credits this call cost. Same total as the `x-elfa-credits` response header,
so a consumer can reconcile from either.

Record_string.unknown_.description: Construct a type with a set of properties K of type T

ApiKeyAutoErrorBody.description: An error passed through as an object, e.g. a failed account lookup or validation.

details.description: Per-field or per-condition details, when present

error.description:
A message string, or an object with `code` and `message` (for example a `503`
when the X account lookup is unavailable: `{ "code": "ERR_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
"message": "ACCOUNT_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE" }`).

ApiKeyAutoErrorEnvelope.description:
An error answered through the API's error handler, with a code and ids to
quote to support. Builder chat answers a message the safety checks rejected
with this, as a `400` with `code: "ERR_BAD_REQUEST"`.

message.example: Your query was flagged by our safety filter and was not processed. You were not charged for it.

details.description: Per-field or per-condition details, when present

errorId.description: Identifies this kind of error, to quote to support

requestId.description: Identifies this request, to quote to support

ApiKeyAutoChatFailedResponse.description:
A Builder chat turn that has no answer: the session was not found (`404`),
or the turn ended without an answer (`502`).

sessionId.description:
The session of the turn, to retry in. Present on the `404` and on a `502`
stream error; absent on the fallback `502`, which carries only `error`.

supported.description: Whether the symbol is supported by the price/TA data source

ApiKeyTweetAccount.description: The X account a `tweet.semantic` condition resolved to, and how it is billed.

path.description: The condition this entry belongs to. Join on this field.

username.description:
The `username` exactly as submitted (trimmed; case and any leading `@` kept), so
it may differ from the account's canonical handle. Join on `path`, not on this.

accountSourceRefId.description: The X account id the username resolved to.

billing.description:
`included`: the account is in Elfa's included real-time set and costs nothing
extra. `per_post`: every post from the account is billed while the query runs.

creditsPerPost.description:
`per_post` only: credits charged to this API key for each post from the account
(posts, quotes, notes and articles; not replies or reposts).

ApiKeyFollowAccount.description:
An X account watched by an `x_follow_made` or `x_follow_overlap` condition, the
account it resolved to, and how it is billed.

path.description:
The condition this entry belongs to. An `x_follow_overlap` condition has one
entry per account, all with the same `path`. Join on `path` and `username`.

username.description: The watched account's username as stored on the query: lowercase, without `@`.

accountSourceRefId.description: The X account id the username resolved to.

billing.description:
`included`: Elfa already reads this account's follows and it costs nothing extra.
`per_day`: billed for each UTC day its follows are read while the query runs.

creditsPerDay.description:
`per_day` only: credits charged to this API key for each day the account's
follows are read.

estimatedCredits.description:
Estimated credits for the query's model calls over its lifetime, from the
simulation. `null` when no estimate can be made. Per-post X account charges and
per-day follow account charges are not included.

tweetAccounts.description:
One entry per `tweet.semantic` condition, with its account and billing. Absent
when the query has no `tweet.semantic` condition or failed an earlier check.

followAccounts.description:
One entry per account an `x_follow_made` or `x_follow_overlap` condition watches,
with its billing. Absent when the query has no such condition, when the key
cannot watch accounts billed per day, or when one of those accounts was rejected.

title.description:
Optional title to validate alongside the query. Accepted so agents can
validate the full create-query payload in one call. See
{@link ApiKeyCreateQueryRequestBody.title}.

description.description:
Optional description to validate alongside the query. See
{@link ApiKeyCreateQueryRequestBody.description}.
description.example: Notify when BTC is above 100k so I can review the breakout setup.

id.description: The new query's id. Use it for poll, stream, cancel and delete.

estimatedCredits.description:
Estimated credits for the query's model calls over its lifetime, as on validate.
`null` when no estimate can be made. Per-post X account charges and per-day
follow account charges are not included.

tweetAccounts.description:
One entry per `tweet.semantic` condition, with its account and billing, as on
validate. Absent when the query has no `tweet.semantic` condition.

followAccounts.description:
One entry per account an `x_follow_made` or `x_follow_overlap` condition watches,
with its billing, as on validate.

title.description:
Short human-readable title for the query.

Surfaced back in outbound notifications (Telegram, webhook, notify) so the
recipient immediately recognizes **what** fired — recipients often see an
alert hours or days after the query was created. Strongly recommended for
agent-built queries.

description.description:
1–2 sentence description of the thesis or intent behind the trigger.

Surfaced alongside the title in outbound notifications so the recipient
understands **why** the trigger was set up. Write it as if the recipient
has forgotten they set this up — because they often have.
description.example: Notify when BTC is above 100k so I can review the breakout setup.

index.description: Zero-based condition index from the flattened EQL condition tree

source.description: Data source that produced the value

args.description: Public condition arguments with internal source identifiers removed

currentValue.description: Latest observed value at evaluation time

targetValue.description: Threshold or comparison value from the EQL condition

isMet.description: Whether this condition was met in the latest evaluation

lastUpdated.description: ISO timestamp for the condition value

reason.description: Optional evaluator explanation or error reason

conversationSessionId.description: Linked LLM conversation session, when the condition used an LLM run

runId.description: Linked Auto/LLM run id, when available

cacheHit.description: Whether the condition value came from cache

evaluatedAt.description: ISO timestamp of the latest evaluation

conditionStates.description: Per-condition values from the latest evaluation snapshot

wouldTriggerNow.description: Whether the latest evaluation would trigger at that time

matchingConditions.description: Number of conditions that matched in the latest evaluation

args.description: Public condition arguments with internal source identifiers removed

value.description: Threshold or comparison value from the EQL condition

ApiKeyAutoFeedSubject.description:
What a kalshi, polymarket or mindshare condition watches, recorded when the
plan was created. Kalshi: title, yesSubTitle, noSubTitle, eventTicker,
closeTime. Polymarket: question, outcome, eventSlug, url, endDate.
Mindshare: name, symbol.

ApiKeyAutoFeedContextValue.description: One fact from the message that fired a feed condition

ApiKeyAutoFeedContext.description:
Public facts from the message that fired a feed condition (kalshi,
polymarket, sec, mindshare, fear_greed, funding, liquidation)

topic.description: Which feed the message came from, e.g. `filings.sec`, `trades.kalshi` or `markets.kalshi`

sourceRecordId.description: The message's id in that feed, e.g. an SEC accession number

fields.description: The message's public fields by name, e.g. companyName, form, items and filingIndexUrl for an SEC filing, or yesPrice and takerOutcomeSide for a Kalshi trade. A field the message lacks is left out.

truncated.description: True when some fields were cut short or left out to fit the size limit

observedValue.description: Numeric/string/boolean value observed when the trigger fired

observedLabel.description: Feed conditions: an enum or boolean reading as written, e.g. "8-K" or "Fear"; observedValue then holds the number the feed sent

subject.description: Feed conditions: what the condition watches. Absent for sources without one and for plans created before it was recorded.

context.description: Feed conditions: public facts from the message that fired the condition

url.description: Public source URL for semantic tweet and Telegram matches, when available; market-event matches have none

mentionedAt.description: Source event timestamp for semantic matches

accountHandle.description: Public account handle of the matched post's author, when available

chatUsername.description: Public Telegram chat username, when available

chatTitle.description: Public Telegram chat title, when available

messageId.description: Public Telegram message id, when available

messageIds.description: Public Telegram grouped message ids, when available

groupId.description: Public Telegram group id, when available

match.description: Public match details, including observedValue for numeric conditions

type.description: Trigger category, e.g. price, poll, cron, or event

time.description: ISO timestamp when the trigger fired

matchedConditions.description: Conditions that were met when the trigger fired

triggerTime.description: ISO timestamp when the Auto query fired

conditionsMet.description: Number of conditions met when the Auto query fired

trigger.description: Canonical public trigger context for why the query fired

message.description: What happened and what to do next, in plain language.

source.description:
Where the failure came from: `billing` (a per-post charge was refused),
`execution`, `query_evaluation`, `pending_setup` or `agent_validation`.

executions.description: List of executions triggered by this query

credits.description: Aggregated LLM credits from sessions linked to this query

failure.description: Present when the query ended as `failed` with a recorded reason.

Carried over when the draft is converted into an active query and then

Surfaced alongside the title in outbound notifications once the draft is

actionSnapshot.description: Action configuration snapshot; returned by the single-execution endpoint

executionContext.description: Execution context with user identity stripped

externalEvents.description: External event records linked to the execution

notificationOutbox.description: Sanitized notification outbox delivery metadata linked to the execution

offset.description: Offset used for the page (offset paging only)

hasMore.description: Whether another page exists. With `after`: whether more executions are ready now; poll again later for newer ones.

nextCursor.description: With `after`: pass it back as `after` to read the executions that follow. Present on every cursor page, including an empty one.

message.description: The user message. Required when analysisType is "chat"; ignored for all other analysis types.

sessionId.description: Omit to start a new conversation. Pass the sessionId from a previous response to continue an existing conversation.

EventClassV3.description: What the event is about: the market at large, one asset, or somebody's call.

ImplicationV3.description: Which way the event cuts. On a call, derived from the side taken.

EventTypeV3.description: What kind of development it is. Anything the model cannot place becomes `other`.

EventCategoryV3.description:
What kind of thing happened, finer than `eventType` and across it: `eventType` is the
domain (`macro`), the category the happening (`economy`, `commentary`, `forecast`).
New values may be added; treat one you do not know as no category.

EntityTypeV3.description: What an entity is. The same values `/v3/entities` takes and returns.

id.description: Family UUID for tokens/equities; entity UUID for every other type.

symbol.description: Ticker on a token or an equity, null on anything else.

AlertActionV3.description: Whether the analyzer flagged the event, or is only watching it.

EventImpactV3.description: A measured price reaction, on one of the event's entities.

entityId.description: Asset family whose measured member moved.

symbol.description: The symbol the price was read under.

priceChange1d.description: Signed return over the day after the event, as a proportion.

movedFirst.description: The price moved before the event was published.

marketWide.description: BTC moved at the same time, so the asset's move may not be about this event.

final.description: The measurement window has closed and the numbers will not change again.

EventCitedSourceV3.description: A post or SEC filing an event cites. Never its text.

source.description:
`twitter`, `telegram` or `sec_edgar` (an SEC filing: a company's 8-K, a
foreign issuer's 6-K, or a Schedule 13D, a holder's 5%+ stake in a
company). Empty when the source cannot be told.

sourceRecordId.description:
The post's id on X; on Telegram, a reference to a group of messages; on
`sec_edgar`, the filing's SEC accession number (`0000104169-26-000165`).

handle.description:
The X account, or the sender's Telegram name. On `sec_edgar`, a company
name as it stands on the SEC record (`Walmart Inc.`, or
`CISCO SYSTEMS, INC.` in capitals), not a social handle: the filer's on
an 8-K or 6-K; on a Schedule 13D, the company whose shares are held, not
the holder who filed it.

link.description:
Permalink where one exists: the X post, or the first message of a Telegram
group in a public chat. Null for a private Telegram chat. On `sec_edgar`,
the document on sec.gov the event was read from: on an 8-K or 6-K, its
press release exhibit when it has one, otherwise the 8-K or 6-K itself; on
a Schedule 13D, the statement itself.

EventPositionsV3.description: Present on a call only. Counts the lifecycle rows behind it.

id.description: The event id. The `id` a caller filters on is an entity id; this is the row.

eventCategory.description:
What kind of thing happened. `null` when the event reports no concrete happening
(chatter, recaps), is not typed yet, or was analysed before 2026-09-30. It can change
when the event is re-analysed.

primaryEntities.description: What the event is about. Named and typed from the registry at read.

relatedEntities.description: Named alongside, but not what the event is about.

originCount.description:
Distinct accounts and filers behind the event: the cited sources', plus,
for a market event, every account or filer whose source joined the
cluster and passed the source gate. A market event's count is read live,
so it grows after `analyzedAt`; a call or asset event's stays at its cited
accounts.

impacts.description: One per entity measured, the event's own subjects first. Empty on most events. Measured after the event and can change while `final` is false.

firstSeenAt.description:
Unix seconds. First post in the cluster, not when the news broke.
On long-lived call clusters this can predate the event by hours.

storylineId.description: The thread this event belongs to. Null on a call.

citedSources.description:
The posts and SEC filings the analysis cited, first and in its order,
then, for a market event, later sources from other accounts that passed
the source gate (posts and SEC filings), one per account or filer, up to
the cap. Never their text.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page. Null on the last page.

StorylineRelationV3.description: How an event relates to the thread it sits in.

material.description: The event added something substantive, rather than restating the thread.

entities.description: Everything the thread is about. Empty on roughly a quarter of threads.

lastEventAt.description: Unix seconds. Moves with every event, including ones that only restate the thread.

lastMaterialAt.description:
Unix seconds: the latest material event the thread shows. The prices and levels the
title and summary state are as of this moment or shortly after, so plot them against
the price then, not now.

arcId.description: Null unless the thread has been grouped into an arc.

PredictionMarketMoveV3.description:
The odds of one outcome an hour before and an hour after a story's first post: of the
market's outcomes priced between 3% and 97% before the story, the one whose move was
most unusual. For a storyline or an arc, across all of its stories.

eventId.description: The story the move is measured around: one of the market's `eventIds`.

outcomeId.description: The outcome's id on its provider: a Polymarket market id or a Kalshi market ticker.

outcome.description: The outcome's question. Null for Kalshi outcomes, and when the name is not known.

before.description: Probability an hour before the story's first post, 0 to 1.

after.description: Probability an hour after the story's first post, 0 to 1.

unusual.description: True when the move is in the top tenth of this market's moves at that time of day over the week before.

marketId.description: The market's id on its provider: a Polymarket event id or a Kalshi event ticker. Unique with `provider`.

closesAt.description: Unix seconds. Null when the provider sets no end, or its date has passed while the market still trades.

eventIds.description: The item's events that link this market, oldest first.

move.description: How the odds moved around one of those stories. Null when none was measured.

CalendarCategoryV3.description: What kind of occasion a calendar entry is.

CalendarStatusV3.description:
`past` is over with nothing reporting it happened; `occurred` is over and
`outcome` names the event that reported it.

CalendarConfidenceV3.description: `official` from the project or issuer, `reported` by others, `rumored` unconfirmed.

startsAt.description: Unix seconds. A `day` entry starts at 00:00 UTC of `date`.

endsAt.description: Unix seconds, or null for a single moment or day.

precision.description: `exact` has a time of day; `day` names the day only.

date.description: `day` precision only: the announced day, YYYY-MM-DD, in no time zone.

endDate.description: `day` precision only: the last day of a span, inclusive.

timezone.description: IANA zone the time was announced in, e.g. `America/New_York`.

importance.description: 0 to 100: how much widely held markets plan around the date.

eventIds.description: Events within the plan's history that reported the date, oldest first. Fetch them with `/v3/events?eventIds=`.

outcome.description: The event that reported it happened, once linked.

MatchedOnV3.description: What the string hit. An id lane scores 1, a symbol 0.9, a loose alias 0.5.

ExternalIdsV3.description: Ids the same thing carries elsewhere. Null on anything the registry does not hold.

figi.description: Composite FIGI where we hold one, otherwise the share class FIGI.

id.description: Family UUID for tokens/equities; entity UUID for every other type.

handle.description: The X account linked to this entity, if one is. Handles change; the id does not.

barAt.description: Unix seconds. Sealed hours, except the newest row, which is a live tick.

longShare.description: 0 to 100. How many of the counted accounts are long.

shortShare.description: 0 to 100. The two add up, because an evenly split account does not vote.

crowdingPercentile.description: 0 to 100. Where the lean sits among this book's last 28 days, so 50 is typical.

pulse24.description: 0 to 100. How unusual the last day's new calls are against this book's history.

pulse24LongShare.description: 0 to 100. How many of those new calls were long.

computedAt.description: Unix seconds. When this bar (or live tick) was last written.

Pick_CallAssetV3.Exclude_keyofCallAssetV.description: From T, pick a set of properties whose keys are in the union K

CallActionV3.description: What the author did to the position.

CallSetupV3.description: What the call was read off. Null when the author did not say.

CallThesisV3.description: What the author expected to drive it. Null when they did not say.

channel.description: A Telegram channel's title. Null for a post in a group chat we cannot name.

CallDirectionV3.description: Which way an account is positioned.

CallHorizonV3.description: How long the author meant to hold it. Sets when the call expires.

CloseReasonV3.description: Why a call ended. `expiry` is us closing it, the rest are the author.

CallerTrackV3.description:
An account's record over every position it has opened, in every market and since
scoring began, not cut to the plan's history. Scored once a day from closed
positions; the scores are null until an account has a scored one.

alphaScore.description:
-1 to 1. How well the scored positions did, blending their return against the
market (BTC for crypto, SPY for equities), their realized return, how much of the
move they kept and how they exited; averaged, then pulled toward 0 while there are
few, so a handful of lucky calls cannot outrank many solid ones.

hitRate.description: 0 to 1. The share of scored positions that made money.

avgReturn.description: The mean realized return of scored positions, direction-adjusted, as a fraction (0.05 is 5%).

totalEpisodes.description: Every position the account has opened.

channel.description: A Telegram channel's title. Null for a post in a group chat we cannot name.

openedAt.description: Unix seconds. When the author posted.

setup.description:
From the opening call; null when it gave none, the position opened another way, or
the opening call is older than the plan's history.

statedTarget.description: Prices the author named when opening, if any; null as for `setup`.

track.description: The author's record across all their positions.

calls.description:
The calls inside the plan's history, oldest first. Empty when every call on a
position still open in range is older than that.

standing.description: 0 to 1, against every account we score. What `metric=standing` ranks by.

track.description: Null when the account has never opened a position.

AccountMetricV3.description:
Which axis an account is ranked on. `standing` is influence; `alphaScore`, `hitRate`
and `avgReturn` are its record as a caller, the same numbers as its `track`.

standing.description: 0 to 1, against every account we score.

standingRaw.description: Decayed inbound engagement, unbounded. What the percentile is computed from.

AccountAssociationV3.description: What a bio states, not what we verified.

get.description:
Returns the most significant mentions for a given ticker symbol, ranked by
engagement (viewCount → mentionedAt → relevance) within a specified time
window.

**Response shape.** The response envelope is `{ success, data, metadata }`.
`data` is a flat array of mentions; pagination state lives in `metadata`
(`total`, `page`, `pageSize`) — never merged into the top level.

**No tweet content.** V2 does not return raw tweet text. Use the `link`
field to fetch the original tweet via the Twitter/X API if needed, or use
the SDK's `fetchRawTweets: true` option with a Twitter bearer token.

**No account object.** Unlike `/v2/data/keyword-mentions`, this endpoint
does not return an `account` object per mention.

**Field notes.** `mentionedAt` is an ISO 8601 string (not a unix
timestamp). `repostBreakdown.smart` counts reposts by smart accounts;
`repostBreakdown.ct` counts reposts by crypto-Twitter accounts.

parameters.description: The ticker symbol to get mentions for. Use `$` prefix (e.g., `$SOL` or URL-encoded `%24SOL`) for exact cashtag matching only. Without `$`, results include both cashtag mentions and general token references.

get.description:
Search mentions by keywords OR account name within a time period. Either
`keywords` or `accountName` (or both) must be provided.

**Response shape.** The response envelope is `{ success, data, metadata }`.
`data` is a flat array of mentions; pagination state lives in `metadata`.

**Cursor pagination.** Unlike `/v2/data/top-mentions` (which uses
`page`/`pageSize`), this endpoint is cursor-paginated.
`metadata.cursor` is a millisecond timestamp (number). To fetch the next
page, pass its value back as the `cursor` query param. Page until `data`
is empty; `metadata.cursor` is only omitted on that empty page.
`metadata.total` is the complete matching result set, not the remainder
after the cursor, and may be capped at 10000 for performance.

**No tweet content.** V2 does not return raw tweet text. Use the `link`
field to fetch the original tweet via the Twitter/X API if needed, or use
the SDK's `fetchRawTweets: true` option with a Twitter bearer token.

**Account info.** Each mention includes a minimal `account` object with
only `username` and `isVerified`. No id, display name, follower count, or
bio is returned.

**Field notes.** `mentionedAt` is an ISO 8601 string (not a unix
timestamp). `repostBreakdown.smart` counts reposts by smart accounts;
`repostBreakdown.ct` counts reposts by crypto-Twitter accounts.

post.description:
Send a message to the Elfa AI and receive a complete response.
Suited for agents and integrations that do not support server-sent events (SSE).

**Analysis types and required fields:**
- `chat` (default) — general conversation. Requires `message`.
- `macro` — macro market overview. No `message` needed.
- `summary` — quick market summary. No `message` needed.
- `tokenIntro` — token introduction. Requires `assetMetadata` with `symbol`, or `chain` + `contractAddress`.
- `tokenAnalysis` — token trade setup analysis. Same `assetMetadata` requirements as `tokenIntro`.
- `accountAnalysis` — Twitter/X account analysis. Requires `assetMetadata.username`.

`message` is only used for `analysisType: "chat"` and is ignored for other
analysis types. `adaptive` speed is not available on x402.

Send `includeSources: true` to receive `data.sources`: the links the
research behind the answer read, with a `kind` each. Links only: page and
post content is not returned.

**`assetMetadata` fields (when applicable):**
- `symbol` — token ticker symbol (e.g. `"BTC"`, `"$ETH"`)
- `chain` — blockchain name (e.g. `"ethereum"`, `"solana"`)
- `contractAddress` — token contract address
- `username` — Twitter/X username for account analysis

**Cost:** speed based. Pay a flat price per turn with the `exact` scheme
(`fast` $1, `expert` $2). Where the 402 also lists `batch-settlement`
(Base), you can instead deposit once into a payment channel: each turn is
then capped at `fast` $2 / `expert` $6 and charged only what it cost.
Requires x402 payment.

get.description:
What is scheduled: launches, unlocks, votes, listings, earnings, data releases, rate
decisions, hearings, conferences and deadlines, across crypto, equities and macro.
Soonest first, with a cursor. Each entry keeps its schedule: `status` says when it was
moved, postponed or cancelled, and once it is over, `outcome` names the event that
reported it happened. `eventIds` are the events within the plan's history that
reported the date.

Unlike the other lists, the default range reads ahead: `from` defaults to 00:00 UTC
today (or 30 days before `to` when `to` is earlier), and `to` to 30 days after
`from`. Both are inclusive, and an entry that started earlier but is still running at
`from` is listed too. A range that starts before the plan's history is cut, and
`servedFrom` says where it started. Entries reach about 400 days ahead.

A `day` entry names a day, not a moment: read `date`, which never shifts with a time
zone. `importance` scores how much widely held markets (BTC, ETH, large caps, rates,
FX) plan around the date. 80 and up, unless postponed or cancelled, is what the Elfa
app calls Key: about two a day.

Cost: 1 credit, plus 1 per entry not already billed to the account that UTC day.
Errors cost nothing.

parameters.description: Repeatable, or comma separated. Default every status.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: 0 to 100. `80` keeps Key entries; postponed or cancelled ones keep their score.

tags.name: v2 Auto
tags.description:
Conditional query builder and runner: create, validate, poll, and stream EQL queries, and manage LLM sessions.

**Required Sequence (Enforced)**
1. `POST /v2/auto/queries/validate`
2. `POST /v2/auto/queries`
3. `POST /v2/auto/queries/{queryId}/cancel` (only while status is `active`)
4. `DELETE /v2/auto/queries/{queryId}` (only after status is terminal: `triggered`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `failed`)

**Intent Routing (Strict)**

| User intent | Required source | Required fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account-anchored post intent (`@user posted ...`) | `source: "tweet"` | `args.username` (no `@`), `args.text`, `args.minConfidence` (start at `80`) |
| One account's trading calls (`@user opens a long`, `@user exits BTC`) | `source: "calls"` | `args.handle` (no `@`); optional `args.asset`, `args.direction`, `args.action` |
| News or world event intent (`ETF approved`, exploit, listing, bearish news on ETH) | `source: "events"` | At least one filter (`args.entity`, `args.eventType`, `args.implication`, …) or `args.text` + `args.minConfidence` (start at `80`) |
| Fuzzy world-state predicate not naturally post/event matching | `source: "llm"` | `method: "athena_condition"`, `args.query`, `args.period` (`>= 1h`) |
